subject: Trilogy MSA: derivative output custody vs license - logistics
messages:
From: Sam Mason <sam.mason@trilogy.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, procurement@trilogy.com
Cc: Asha Patel <asha.patel@trilogy.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Apr 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Trilogy MSA & Order Form - redline (derivative/output clauses)

Laura – attaching Trilogy’s redlines to the MSA and Order Form annex. A few items we need clarity on immediately:

- Section 7.2 (Output ownership): Trilogy is proposing assignment of customer-generated output where the output is directly derived from our proprietary prompts/data. We flagged this because our procurement policy requires clear assignment language for productized outputs.
- Training / feedback (Sec 9.1): We’ve retained language that permits Redwood to use de-identified feedback for model improvements; Trilogy requires an opt-out flow and a covenant that PII or customer proprietary datasets won’t be used without express consent.
- Derivative/Downstream use: We redlined an explicit carveout for productization (customer may require exclusive downstream rights for certain named features).

Can you confirm Redwood’s position and whether you can accept the assignment language (or propose license-based alternatives)? We’d like to lock these clauses before legal provides the final signoff to procurement.

Attachments: Trilogy_redline_MSA_20290328.pdf, Trilogy_OrderForm_AnnexA_redline.docx

Thanks,
Sam Mason
Sr. Counsel, Trilogy

Sam — thanks for sending. I’ve looped in our commercial and legal partners to review (Ben Carter and Rishi Malhotra). We want to be pragmatic here: Redwood’s standard is to grant a nonexclusive service-based license to outputs while offering narrow assignment for narrowly-defined productization scenarios with explicit payment/commitments.

Next steps from our side:
- Internal review this AM; Ben will propose counter language for Sec 7.2 that preserves your ability to productize named features with a limited carveout.
- Rishi will scope acceptable language for training/feedback opt-out and a sample consent flow.
- Can we schedule a quick 30-min call Wed morning PT to triage the remaining redlines and sign off on an MMP (mutual action plan)?

We’ll send a proposed counter (tracked) by EOD Tuesday.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Director, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com


From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, irene.choi@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 01 Apr 2029 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Trilogy MSA & Order Form - redline (derivative/output clauses)

Laura / team — quick internal notes while I draft counter: 

1) Output custody vs license (Sec 7.2): Trilogy asks for assignment where output is “directly derived” from their data. That’s very broad. Recommend we propose the following path:
   - For general outputs (responses, content) Redwood grants a perpetual, worldwide, nonexclusive license to use, reproduce, and display outputs generated for Trilogy.
   - For Productization Assignment: allow Trilogy to request assignment for specific, named deliverables (e.g., model-integrated feature X) subject to: a) a defined Purchase Order / additional consideration, b) mutually agreed acceptance criteria, and c) a limited set of examples/evidence demonstrating derivation.

2) Training & feedback (Sec 9.1): we can accept an opt-out and a stricter PII covenant. Proposed language: Redwood will not include Trilogy-provided PII or sensitive datasets in model training unless Trilogy provides express written consent. For feedback, Redwood may use aggregated/de-identified feedback for continuous improvements; Trilogy can opt-out of feedback collection for selected projects via a configuration flag on the service.

3) Telemetry/attribution: if Trilogy requires attribution or metadata tagging in downstream products, we need to ensure it doesn’t leak operational telemetry. Propose a joint playbook for evidence and audits.

I’ll convert this into tracked changes and attach our suggested redline by EOD. Irene — can you pull any past examples of assignment language we used (Novum/Acme) and flag pitfalls?

—Ben
Director, Legal Ops | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com


From: laura.bennett@redwood.com <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sam Mason <sam.mason@trilogy.com>, Asha Patel <asha.patel@trilogy.com>, procurement@trilogy.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Apr 2029 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Trilogy MSA: Redwood proposed counters (derivative output & training)

Sam / Asha — thanks for the patience. Attached is Redwood’s proposed counter-redline (Redwood_proposed_counter_redline.docx) and a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that captures signoff owners and target dates (20 business day SLA to execute final MSA once language agreed). Highlights: 

1) Output custody vs license (Sec 7.2) — compromise language: Redwood grants Trilogy a perpetual, worldwide, nonexclusive license to Outputs. Trilogy may request assignment of title for up to 3 specifically-identified Deliverables per Order Form (must be described in Annex A and accompanied by commercial consideration). Assignment requests trigger a 45-day technical review window to validate derivation.

2) Training / feedback (Sec 9.1) — Redwood agrees not to include Trilogy PII or customer-proprietary datasets in model training without express written consent. For telemetry/feedback, Redwood will provide an opt-out flag at the project (Order Form) level; if Trilogy opts out, Redwood will not use that project’s feedback for model improvement. Redwood will provide quarterly attestations describing the provenance of datasets used for training if requested under NDA.

3) Evidence & audits — proposed limited-evidence path: Trilogy can request samples to validate derivation; audits will be scoped, executed under NDA, and limited to no more than one audit per 12 months unless material breach suspected.

Next steps:
- Please review the attached tracked counter and MAP. If these principles look acceptable we can run a narrow redline call Thurs 10:00 AM PT to agree language and update procurement.
- Attachments: Redwood_proposed_counter_redline.docx, Trilogy_MAP_proposed.pdf

If you prefer we can instead provide a license-first alternative (no assignment at all) with expanded commercial credits — let me know.

Best regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Director, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
